{"question_target":"T06","reply":"No—they’re not the same thing. Medicare Advantage is an alternative way to get Medicare: a private plan provides Parts A and B instead of getting those through Original Medicare. Medigap is different: it’s a supplement that works with Original Medicare to help with your share of certain costs. It does not go with Medicare Advantage. A simple way to picture it is:
Original Medicare → may add Medigap + separate drug plan
Medicare Advantage → private plan for A and B, and most plans include drug coverage
So for your mother, since she has Original Medicare now, Medigap is the one that pairs with it.","question":"Are there doctors or hospitals she definitely wants to keep?
